answer: Anchor standing to one damaged archive from the registry atlas and assigned to no second identity. The applicant restores it fragment by fragment in hash-chained order, each recovered fragment unlocking the next, so one archive admits no parallel crew and no shared labour. Halfway through, a sonnet buried inside must be rebuilt line by line from scattered shards, and any copied line breaks the chain. Only restored fragments rebuild the kernel index, proving custody. One identity costs 35 hours of forensic work; 10,000 cost 350,000 hours, and no purchased restoration covers a second archive.
